subject: Complete WVB 1.39 verification without runtime admission
claim: The complete compiler-aligned verifier accepts the published immutable Option/Result candidate only after semantic, typed/loan, and control-flow checks. The existing metadata and typed-stack matrices now check complete-entry-point rejection and phase results. All 305 focused owner groups pass on Windows and Debian with identical WVB output.

source.value: Worktree based on d1df6eb31507194e60da826fd5e8da81af166658; exact changed implementation and fixture identities below.

runs.target: 305 Foundation owner groups, including complete-verifier assertions in the 37 metadata and 120 typed-stack groups

limitations: Only the blanket minor-39 rejection was removed from production code. All existing semantic, typed/loan, control-flow, metadata normalization, version, authority, and resource checks remain in the same entry path.
The first runs used a fixture still expecting the old complete-admission rejection and failed with status 165 on both hosts. The corrected fixture produced the final passing runs.

Verification is not execution admission. The scalar envelope still rejects minor 39; runtime execution, native lowering, installed tools, consumer migration, and full compiler/library qualification remain pending.
The focused owner executes current verifier source, not a promoted standalone verifier executable. Existing immutable bootstrap and installed-tool identities were not changed.

PlanOnly conservatively selected nine owners with 2550 expected seconds. The focused owner was selected for the version-39-only branch change; unrelated seed, database, library, and application suites were not rerun. An earlier-version regression remains in the selected metadata owner.
The group count is unchanged: existing focused cases gained complete-entry-point assertions rather than adding a duplicate verifier.
